annotations.text:
CHOSE A — Evidence beside decision.

The queue exists to turn a reviewer's judgement into ground truth, so a verdict reached without looking at the page is worse than no verdict at all: A is the only direction that makes the crop impossible to skip, and keyboard triage buys back the density it costs.

B stays the right answer once the resolver has earned trust and volume dominates. C is the arbitration view for a contested item.

The crop panels here are drawn placeholders, not page images. SPEC ground rule 0 forbids copying document content into the repo outside output/, and a committed artboard is inside the repo. The running app renders the real crop server-side from the bbox via PyMuPDF at request time.

Palette and type are lifted from diagram/Main.dc.html, so the trust gradient means the same thing here as on the architecture canvas: blue deterministic, teal rule derived, amber model derived, purple human. A row's left edge tells you which tier proposed it; every control that records a human verdict is purple.
